FINAL IVX AUTONOMOUS SENIOR DEVELOPER CUTOVER
COMPLETE THE CODING LOOP, SYNC IVX IA CHAT, DEPLOY, AND VERIFY WITH REAL EVIDENCE

EXECUTE NOW — DO NOT RETURN A PLAN
DO NOT MARK COMPLETE FROM UNIT TESTS ALONE
DO NOT CLAIM “AUTONOMOUS” UNTIL A LIVE JOB WRITES, TESTS, REVISES, COMMITS, DEPLOYS, AND VERIFIES CODE WITHOUT RORK AUTHORING THE PATCH

==================================================
CURRENT VERIFIED STATE
==================================================

The following capabilities already exist or are partially implemented:

- IVX IA Chat intent routing
- Persistent worker jobs
- Structured task IDs and status URLs
- Read-only repository inspection
- Honest execution and contradiction guards
- Autonomous-coder loop implementation
- Owner-controlled LLM gateway and API credential binding
- Owner-controlled GitHub commit path
- Owner-controlled Render deployment path
- Supabase-backed job queue
- Unit-tested inspect → plan → patch → test → revise → verify → commit flow
- Chat-to-worker routing for code-change tasks

The current live pilot is incomplete because it remained in the LLM planning stage and did not produce a valid patch, commit, deployment, or production verification during the observed execution window.

This task must close that final gap.

==================================================
FINAL OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Make IVX IA Chat the real owner-controlled senior-developer interface:

Owner request
→ classify intent
→ create exactly one persistent job
→ inspect repository
→ generate technical plan
→ generate valid patch
→ apply patch in isolated workspace
→ run targeted tests
→ analyze failures
→ revise patch
→ run typecheck and regression
→ create commit
→ push owner-controlled GitHub
→ request owner approval when required
→ deploy owner-controlled Render/EAS
→ verify production
→ return proof in IVX IA Chat

No Rork agent may manually author the pilot patch.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FIX THE STALLED LLM PLANNING STAGE
==================================================

Audit the live autonomous-coder job that remained at:

RUNNING
Stage: LLM planning
Progress: approximately 10%

Identify the exact failure:

- model request timeout
- malformed model response
- response truncation
- invalid JSON
- schema rejection
- patch parser failure
- content filter
- token limit
- gateway disconnect
- retry-loop defect
- worker heartbeat defect
- queue lease expiration
- unresolved model name
- missing completion event
- task-state persistence failure

Return:

- task ID
- model request ID
- start timestamp
- duration
- HTTP status
- sanitized response metadata
- parser error
- retry count
- last heartbeat
- exact file and line where progression stopped

Do not infer. Use runtime evidence.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — MAKE MODEL OUTPUT DETERMINISTIC
==================================================

The coding-model response must use one strict schema:

{
  "summary": "string",
  "rootCause": "string",
  "filesToInspect": ["path"],
  "edits": [
    {
      "file": "path",
      "operation": "replace | insert | delete | create",
      "search": "exact existing text when required",
      "content": "replacement or new content",
      "reason": "string"
    }
  ],
  "tests": ["command"],
  "risk": "low | medium | high",
  "requiresOwnerApproval": false
}

Implement:

- JSON-schema validation
- safe JSON extraction from fenced output
- repair of minor formatting errors
- maximum response-size handling
- bounded retries
- clear rejection reason
- raw model response logging with secrets removed
- response checksum
- deterministic fallback for the pilot task

Do not silently remain in PLANNING.

If the model does not return a valid response within the allowed attempts:

STATUS: BLOCKED
ERROR CODE: LLM_PLAN_INVALID
include exact evidence.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — IMPLEMENT THE PILOT FALLBACK
==================================================

For the controlled pilot only, add a deterministic fallback so the loop can be proven even if the LLM response is malformed.

Pilot request:

“Change the visible version label AUTONOMOUS-CODER-PILOT-1 to AUTONOMOUS-CODER-PILOT-2. Run targeted tests and typecheck, create a commit, but do not deploy.”

The engine must:

1. Search the repository for the exact label.
2. Require exactly one safe source match or return BLOCKED.
3. Replace only that match.
4. Produce a real diff.
5. Run the relevant targeted test.
6. Run typecheck.
7. Create a commit.
8. Do not deploy.

The fallback must be limited to explicitly safe, exact replacement tasks. It must not become a general uncontrolled editing mechanism.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — COMPLETE THE LIVE PILOT
==================================================

Run the pilot again from IVX IA Chat.

Required progression:

RECEIVED
→ AUTHORIZED
→ QUEUED
→ CLAIMED
→ INSPECTING
→ PLANNING
→ PATCHING
→ TESTING
→ TYPECHECKING
→ VERIFYING
→ COMMITTING
→ COMPLETED

Required evidence:

- one task ID
- one idempotency key
- one worker
- isolated workspace
- starting commit SHA
- exact file found
- exact before value
- exact after value
- real unified diff
- files changed
- targeted test command and exit code
- typecheck command and exit code
- commit SHA
- GitHub push result
- no deployment
- final task status COMPLETED
- chat displays the same task evidence

Do not accept a unit-test simulation as the live pilot.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — FIX JOB HEARTBEAT AND TIMEOUT CONTROL
==================================================

Every running job must update:

- lastHeartbeatAt
- currentStage
- currentStep
- progressPercent
- iteration
- modelRequestId
- workerId

Implement stage-specific time limits:

- queue claim
- inspection
- model planning
- patch application
- targeted tests
- typecheck
- commit
- deployment
- production verification

If a stage exceeds its limit:

1. cancel the hanging operation;
2. record the exact timeout;
3. retry when safe;
4. resume from the last checkpoint;
5. mark BLOCKED after the maximum retries.

Never leave a job indefinitely RUNNING at 10%.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — LIVE SELF-REPAIR TEST
==================================================

After the pilot completes, run a controlled self-repair task.

Use a dedicated test fixture or isolated branch.

Required behavior:

1. Generate or apply an initial patch that causes one targeted test to fail.
2. Capture the exact failure.
3. Send the failure back into the repair stage.
4. Generate a revised patch.
5. Apply the revised patch.
6. Rerun the failed test.
7. Run typecheck.
8. Commit only after all gates pass.

Required proof:

- task ID
- iteration 1 diff
- iteration 1 failure
- model analysis
- iteration 2 diff
- iteration 2 passing tests
- final commit SHA
- no manual Rork-authored correction

This proves the loop can revise its own work.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — REAL CHAT BUG FIX
==================================================

After the pilot and self-repair tests pass, submit this real task through IVX IA Chat:

“Reproduce and fix the chat ordering issue so the most recently active conversation opens first, the latest messages appear correctly, old conversations do not open by default, and loading remains bounded. Run targeted tests, typecheck, commit, request deployment approval, deploy, and verify on Android.”

The autonomous coder must independently:

- inspect the chat files;
- reproduce the defect;
- identify the root cause;
- generate the patch;
- add or update regression tests;
- run tests;
- revise if needed;
- run typecheck;
- create a commit;
- request owner deployment approval;
- deploy after approval;
- verify production.

Rork must not author the patch.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — SYNC IVX IA CHAT TO THE CODER
==================================================

All these intents must create a real autonomous-coder job:

- fix
- build
- implement
- refactor
- audit and fix
- test and fix
- deploy
- create module
- create app
- modify code
- senior developer
- autonomous coder

Read-only intents must create a real read-only worker job:

- inspect
- audit only
- diagnose
- report status
- do not change
- do not deploy

The chat must never answer an execution request with a narrative plan.

Immediate response:

HTTP 202

{
  "taskId": "...",
  "status": "QUEUED",
  "mode": "CODE_CHANGE | READ_ONLY",
  "statusUrl": "...",
  "createdAt": "..."
}

==================================================
PHASE 9 — LIVE CHAT PROGRESS
==================================================

Display real events from the persistent job ledger:

- task accepted
- worker claimed
- inspecting files
- generating plan
- patch generated
- patch applied
- test running
- test failed
- revising patch
- typecheck running
- commit created
- awaiting owner approval
- deploying
- verifying production
- completed or blocked

Do not invent percentages.

Every displayed event must map to a stored job event ID and timestamp.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — ONE AUTHORITATIVE STATE
==================================================

Use one persistent job record and one terminal state.

Allowed terminal states:

COMPLETED
BLOCKED
FAILED
CANCELLED
ROLLED_BACK

A task may not be simultaneously completed and blocked.

Status must come from structured fields, never from natural-language word scanning.

Every task must produce one final chat card.

Deduplicate using:

taskId + terminalStatus

==================================================
PHASE 11 — OWNER APPROVAL GATES
==================================================

Allow autonomous execution for:

- repository inspection
- patch generation
- isolated file changes
- tests
- typecheck
- lint
- local builds
- commit creation

Require owner approval for:

- protected-branch push if configured
- production deployment
- destructive migration
- production-data deletion
- DNS changes
- payment configuration
- credential rotation
- rollback with data risk

The chat must show:

APPROVE
REJECT

Approval must update the same task.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — COST AND RESOURCE CONTROLS
==================================================

Implement per-job controls:

- maximum model tokens
- maximum model calls
- maximum repair iterations
- maximum runtime
- maximum test runtime
- maximum deployment attempts
- cost estimate
- actual model usage
- cancellation
- queue concurrency
- per-repository lock

If a budget is exceeded:

STATUS: BLOCKED
ERROR CODE: BUDGET_LIMIT
include usage evidence.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — SECURITY CONTROLS
==================================================

The autonomous coder must not:

- print secrets
- send secret values to logs
- modify secret stores without approval
- push directly to unauthorized repositories
- execute destructive shell commands outside the workspace
- edit files outside the assigned repository
- bypass branch protections
- deploy without approval
- modify financial records

Use:

- isolated workspace
- command allowlist
- path restrictions
- sanitized logs
- owner authorization
- task-scoped credentials
- audit ledger

==================================================
PHASE 14 — DEPLOYMENT PIPELINE
==================================================

Required production path:

IVX IA Chat
→ IVX Job API
→ IVX Autonomous Coder
→ Owner GitHub
→ Owner Render/EAS
→ Production
→ IVX Verification

No normal coding or deployment request may require:

- Rork UI
- Rork sandbox
- Rork API
- Rork repository proxy
- Rork deploy hook
- Rork-owned credential

Rork may implement this final fix, but the completed runtime must not depend on Rork.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
==================================================

For the real chat fix, verify:

- GitHub HEAD
- Render deployment commit
- runtime `/health` commit
- Android APK/update source commit

All must match.

Run on the production Android application:

- open IVX Chat;
- confirm newest conversation opens first;
- confirm latest message is visible;
- confirm history remains available;
- confirm no old conversation opens incorrectly;
- confirm no duplicate messages;
- confirm no crash;
- confirm loading is improved.

Record screenshots, logs, and timestamps.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — FAILURE AND ROLLBACK
==================================================

Before deployment:

- record stable production commit;
- record stable deployment ID;
- preserve the previous APK/update;
- verify rollback command or action.

If production verification fails:

1. mark task VERIFYING_FAILED;
2. trigger approved rollback;
3. confirm stable production restored;
4. preserve failed-job evidence;
5. do not mark COMPLETED.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — REQUIRED AUTOMATED TESTS
==================================================

Add and run tests for:

1. Valid structured LLM plan.
2. Malformed JSON model response.
3. Truncated model response.
4. Model timeout.
5. Model retry and recovery.
6. Exact-replacement fallback pilot.
7. Patch parser rejection.
8. Patch application failure.
9. Targeted test failure.
10. Successful repair iteration.
11. Typecheck failure.
12. Commit creation.
13. GitHub push failure.
14. Owner approval required.
15. Deployment rejection.
16. Production verification failure.
17. Rollback.
18. Duplicate chat submission.
19. Job restart and resume.
20. One terminal status.
21. Evidence belongs to the same task.
22. Read-only mode cannot edit.
23. Code-change mode can edit.
24. No deployment when prompt says do not deploy.
25. Chat receives final evidence from the job ledger.

Run:

- autonomous-coder unit tests
- worker integration tests
- chat routing tests
- job-state tests
- typecheck
- lint
- backend test suite
- production smoke tests

==================================================
PHASE 18 — REQUIRED EVIDENCE
==================================================

AUTONOMOUS ENGINE

- files changed
- model schema
- parser behavior
- timeout policy
- retry policy
- deterministic fallback
- tests

LIVE PILOT

- task ID
- job events
- starting SHA
- exact diff
- files changed
- commands
- tests
- typecheck
- commit SHA
- GitHub push evidence
- deployment: not requested
- final status

SELF-REPAIR

- task ID
- first failing patch
- failure output
- revised patch
- passing output
- final commit

REAL CHAT FIX

- task ID
- root cause
- autonomous patch
- files changed
- targeted tests
- typecheck
- commit SHA
- owner approval event
- Render deployment ID
- EAS build/update ID
- production screenshots
- Android logs

INFRASTRUCTURE

- owner-controlled model provider
- owner-controlled worker
- owner-controlled GitHub
- owner-controlled queue
- owner-controlled deployment
- zero Rork runtime dependency

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

Do not call IVX IA a real senior developer until all are true:

[ ] The live pilot produces a valid patch.
[ ] The live pilot changes the correct file.
[ ] Targeted tests pass.
[ ] Typecheck passes.
[ ] A real commit is created.
[ ] The commit is pushed by IVX’s worker.
[ ] No Rork agent manually authors the patch.
[ ] A live self-repair task revises a failed patch.
[ ] The real chat bug is fixed by IVX IA.
[ ] IVX IA requests owner approval for deployment.
[ ] Deployment occurs through owner-controlled infrastructure.
[ ] Production verification passes.
[ ] Chat shows live structured progress.
[ ] One message creates one job.
[ ] One job has one terminal state.
[ ] Evidence belongs to the same task.
[ ] Jobs survive restart.
[ ] Cost and iteration limits are enforced.
[ ] Rollback is proven.
[ ] GitHub, Render, runtime, and APK commits match.
[ ] Rork is not required for normal coding.

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

OVERALL STATUS:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

AUTONOMOUS CODER:
LIVE VERIFIED / UNIT-TESTED ONLY / FAILED

IVX IA CHAT SYNC:
PASS / FAIL

LIVE PILOT:
Task ID:
Starting SHA:
Files changed:
Tests:
Typecheck:
Commit SHA:
GitHub push:
Deployment:
Final status:

SELF-REPAIR:
Task ID:
Iterations:
Initial failure:
Final tests:
Commit SHA:
Result:

REAL CHAT FIX:
Task ID:
Root cause:
Files changed:
Tests:
Typecheck:
Commit SHA:
Owner approval:
Render deployment ID:
EAS build/update ID:
Android verification:

COMMIT PARITY:
GitHub HEAD:
Render:
Runtime:
APK/update:
Match: TRUE / FALSE

RORK REQUIRED FOR NORMAL CODING:
YES / NO

FINAL STATUS:
IVX IA IS A LIVE VERIFIED AUTONOMOUS SENIOR DEVELOPER
or
PARTIAL — LIST THE EXACT REMAINING FAILURE WITH TECHNICAL EVIDENCE

Do not return another “implemented” report based only on unit tests.

The final proof must show a live IVX-originated code change, autonomous repair, owner-gated deployment, and production verification.
